docs.title: Architecture Decision Records
docs.text:
ADRs capture the why behind significant, hard-to-reverse decisions — the context, the choice, and what it costs us. They are immutable once accepted: to change a decision, write a new ADR that supersedes the old one rather than editing history.

# Decision Status 0001 JWT access + rotating refresh tokens Accepted 0002 Unified renderer orchestration with pluggable backends Accepted 0003 Duration-aware stream-token TTL for Cast Accepted 0004 Two Cast control paths (server-driven + device-direct) Accepted 0005 Two-phase library scan (scan, then enrich) Accepted 0006 Optional renderer capabilities (queue ownership, staging, pairing, output) Accepted 0007 AirPlay/RAOP via pyatv: evaluated on hardware, not built Accepted 0008 Fire TV: no Fling; Matter Casting not viable for a server today Proposed 0009 DLNA server and renderer-bridge roles: arbitration first Proposed 0010 Continuous-stream mode for seamless Cast album playback Proposed 0011 Native OpenHome/Linn backend: evaluated, not built Accepted

New ADRs use the next number and the template.

docs.title: ADR-0001: JWT access + rotating refresh tokens
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2025 (auth rebuild)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Jamarr needs to secure its API as the real boundary — any client (web, TUI, Android, curl) must authenticate, not just the browser UI. The earlier design used a server-side jamarr_session cookie, which is browser-centric and awkward for non-browser clients and for <audio>/EventSource requests that can't set headers. We wanted something homelab-simple (no full OIDC/SSO) without the common foot-guns (long-lived tokens in localStorage, no revocation).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use two tokens:

  • Access token — short-lived JWT (default 10 min), sent as Authorization: Bearer. Stateless; validated by signature + claims. Kept in memory on the web client, never in localStorage.
  • Refresh token — opaque, long-lived (default 21 days), rotating (each refresh revokes the previous), stateful (stored hashed in auth_refresh_session, so sessions are revocable and multi-session). Delivered to browsers as an HttpOnly cookie (jamarr_refresh, path /api).

Passwords are hashed with argon2. Login is rate-limited (slowapi). The legacy jamarr_session cookie is ignored. For streaming, a separate short-lived signed URL is used instead of cookie auth (see streaming flow / ADR-0003).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Same Bearer model works for every client — enabled the TUI and Android with no redesign.
  • Stolen access tokens expire fast; refresh reuse hard-fails (401) and can be globally revoked per user (/api/auth/logout-all).
  • Cost: clients must implement refresh-on-401, and endpoints that can't send headers (EventSource) authenticate via the refresh cookie instead. (An earlier access_token= query fallback was removed: tokens in URLs leak into proxy logs and browser history.)
  • Stateless access tokens can't be individually revoked before expiry — accepted, given the short TTL.

docs.title: ADR-0002: Unified renderer orchestration with pluggable backends
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-04 (Chromecast refactor, Phase 1)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Playback originally lived in app/api/player.py, which called the UPnPManager singleton directly. Adding Chromecast (and, later, AirPlay or grouped renderers) that way would scatter if kind == "cast" / if kind == "upnp" branches across every player endpoint and the monitor/queue code. Local, server-UPnP, and Android device-UPnP each already had subtly different state ownership.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Introduce a single orchestration layer with pluggable protocol backends (app/services/renderer/):

  • A protocol-neutral contract (RendererBackend, RendererDevice, RendererStatus, RendererCapabilities) every backend implements.
  • A RendererRegistry that routes a canonical renderer_id = "{kind}:{native_id}" to the right backend.
  • A RendererOrchestrator that owns all protocol-neutral behaviour: queue, index, progress, auto-advance, stream/artwork URLs + token policy, and history/Last.fm.
  • Player endpoints depend only on the orchestrator/registry — never on UPnPManager, pychromecast, or protocol libraries.

The two-layer split (backend/provider vs per-device object) and the capability/normalised-status model take inspiration from Music Assistant's provider architecture (reference, not a dependency). Legacy udn input/storage is accepted during migration.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• New protocols (Cast shipped this way; AirPlay/groups are designed-for) add a backend without touching endpoints or the monitor.
  • Orchestration logic is testable with a fake backend, no real devices needed.
  • One API/response shape for all renderers simplifies web/TUI/Android clients.
  • Cost: an extra indirection layer and a migration that carries udn compatibility until all clients move to renderer_id. Worth it for the branching it removes.

docs.title: ADR-0003: Duration-aware stream-token TTL for Cast
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-04 (Chromecast refactor, Phase 1)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Stream URLs carry a short-lived, track-bound JWT (default STREAM_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 300). That works for browser/UPnP playback because the client re-requests a fresh URL per track. A Chromecast receiver parses the URL once and never re-authenticates — a 10-minute track would outlive a 300 s token mid-playback and stall.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Move stream-token TTL selection into the orchestrator (app/services/renderer/token_policy.py) and use a duration-aware TTL for kind == "cast":

min(CAST_STREAM_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS, max(1800, duration_seconds * 2))

CAST_STREAM_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS defaults to 86400 (24 h) as the hard cap; non-Cast playback keeps the 300 s default. Tokens remain bound to track_id (verify_stream_token rejects mismatches), so a leaked Cast URL only plays one track.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Cast playback survives long tracks and pauses without re-auth.
  • Scope stays narrow despite the longer life — one track, one device session.
  • Cost: a leaked Cast URL is replayable for up to its TTL. True revocation would need a token nonce/version store (reissuing a stateless JWT does not invalidate old URLs) — deferred; see Roadmap.
  • Rejected alternative: LAN-allowlist bypass for Cast — breaks the uniform auth model and fails for device-direct Cast where the device IP is unpredictable.

docs.title: ADR-0004: Two Cast control paths (server-driven + device-direct)
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-04 (Chromecast refactor, Phases 2–3)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Chromecast can be controlled two ways, and Jamarr runs in two very different topologies: a home server on the same LAN as the Cast devices, and a public/VPS server reachable from anywhere. A single control path can't serve both — server mDNS discovery fails across networks, and Android can't control Cast devices it can't reach.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Support both control paths, sharing the same renderer contract and stream delivery:

Path Discovers Controls Topology Server-driven server (mDNS, pychromecast) server Cast devices on the server's LAN Device-direct Android (Cast SDK) Android server anywhere, phone + Cast on same Wi-Fi

In both, the Cast device fetches the stream URL from the server over HTTP and plays via the Default Media Receiver — no custom receiver app. Device-direct Cast pins the server's active renderer to local:<clientId> and reports queue/index/progress through the existing local-client path, so history and scrobbling match Android device-UPnP.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Home-server users get zero-config Cast; remote/VPS users still get Cast from their phone.
  • Artwork URLs must be fetchable by the Cast receiver directly, which is why /art/* stays unauthenticated (see Artwork).
  • Device-direct Cast requires Google Play Services — de-Googled Android falls back to server-driven Cast only.
  • Cost: two discovery/control implementations to maintain (server pychromecast
  • Android Cast SDK), kept manageable by the shared RendererBackend / DeviceRendererController contracts (ADR-0002).
  • v1 does not transcode; unsupported codecs fail on the receiver.

docs.title: ADR-0005: Two-phase library scan (scan, then enrich)
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: scanner v3

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A music library scan does two very different kinds of work: reading file tags off disk (fast, local, deterministic) and fetching rich metadata from external APIs (slow, rate-limited, network-dependent — MusicBrainz, Spotify, Last.fm, Fanart.tv, Qobuz). Doing both in one pass means a full scan is gated by the slowest external API, and a transient API failure can stall ingesting files that are already on disk.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Split scanning into two CLI phases (app/scanner/cli.py):

  1. scan — walk the filesystem, extract tags (mutagen), detect changes via mtime, and populate tracks/artists/albums + MusicBrainz IDs. Fast and offline.
  2. metadata — enrich the existing DB from external APIs (bios, artwork, sort names, external links) through the v3 pipeline. Only fills blank fields; never overwrites tag-based names.

prune removes orphans; full runs scan → metadata → prune. Enrichment is built as a planner/executor/stages pipeline (see Scanner Pipeline).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Initial scans are fast and usable immediately; rich metadata fills in on-demand or in the background.
  • External API failures degrade gracefully — they only affect the metadata phase, not file ingestion.
  • Enrichment is re-runnable and filterable (--artist, --mbid, --links-only, --bio-only) without re-walking the filesystem.
  • Cost: a freshly scanned library looks sparse until metadata runs; multi-artist collaborations have blank names until then.

docs.title: ADR-0006: Optional renderer capabilities (queue ownership, staging, pairing, output)
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-28 (#316, "Common contracts")

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ADR-0002 gave every backend one RendererBackend contract and a flat RendererCapabilities bag of booleans.

docs.title: 316 adds devices whose behaviour does not fit that bag:
docs.text:
• Who owns the queue differs. UPnP AVTransport and server Cast play whatever Jamarr loads next (server-owned). OpenHome Playlist and Cast receiver queues hold the playlist on the device (renderer-owned; OpenHome evaluated in ADR-0011). A continuous PCM stream carries many tracks in one HTTP response, so the device never sees a track change.
  • Next-track staging (UPnP SetNextAVTransportURI) works on some renderers and is switched off at runtime on others (app/services/upnp/staging.py).
  • Pairing: AirPlay receivers may demand a PIN pairing or password, and the resulting credentials must persist (ADR-0007).
  • Output limits: rate, bit depth, channels and codecs, which the audio planner needs; MIME strings alone do not carry them.

Two existing flags were also untrue: UPnP supports_events came from discovery and was always true although no GENA subscription existed, and can_enqueue meant nothing on any backend.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Extend app/services/renderer/contracts.py, additively and with defaults that describe a plain server-queue renderer:

Field Values Default queue_ownership server, renderer, continuous_stream server queue_operations subset of read insert delete move clear play_item shuffle repeat (renderer-owned only) empty can_stage_next next track can be handed to the device ahead of time false pairing none, optional, required none has_credentials null when no pairing applies, else whether Jamarr holds them null output {codecs, max_sample_rate_hz, max_bit_depth, max_channels, source} all unknown

output.source says how a limit is known: advertised, protocol, documented or measured. An empty or null limit means unknown, not unlimited.

Optional behaviour lives in runtime_checkable Protocols that backends implement only when the operation works:

  • SupportsNextTrackStaging: next_track_staging_allowed, clear_next_track.
  • SupportsPairing: begin_pairing, finish_pairing, set_password, forget_credentials.
  • SupportsStatusEvents: existing; now runtime-checkable.

backend_supports(backend) lists the optional contracts a backend implements. No shipped backend owns its queue or pairs: the renderer-owned queue and SupportsPairing are contract only, for a future OpenHome or AirPlay backend (ADR-0011, ADR-0007). The queue-editing Protocol itself is left to that backend.

A flag is true only when the operation works through Jamarr now:

  • UPnP can_stage_next uses the same staging_allowed() policy as the monitor, which checks config override, runtime faults and the device advert. supports_events is true only when the manager reports a healthy subscription (UpnpEventManager.supports_events, or the verdict persisted from an earlier run).
  • Cast reports a server-owned queue and Google's documented output limits (FLAC up to 96 kHz/24-bit), with source: documented.
  • The local browser renderer uses the same capability shape.

can_enqueue keeps its old meaning (append to a device-side queue) and stays false everywhere. Staging is the separate can_stage_next flag.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• /api/renderers gains keys inside capabilities. The clients ignore unknown keys: Android's Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true } with a Renderer DTO that does not model capabilities, the web UI and the TUI (which read plain dicts). No client change is needed to keep working.
  • The web player hides pause, seek and mute where can_pause, can_seek or can_mute is false. Android and the TUI do not use the flags yet.
  • Backends that implement a Protocol must keep its flag in step. Tests in tests/unit/test_renderer_contracts.py pin the UPnP and Cast flags.
  • renderer_row_to_api in persistence.py (unused) still builds the old flat dict.

docs.title: ADR-0007: AirPlay/RAOP via pyatv — evaluated, not built
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted (evaluation; no backend ships)
  • Date: 2026-10-29 (#316, Priority 3)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
airplay is a recognised renderer kind with no backend. #316 asks for an independent evaluation covering:

  • URL playback versus streamed audio
  • pairing, passwords and persistent credentials
  • per-device features
  • timing and latency
  • session cleanup
  • receiver generations, seeking, gapless playback and multiroom

The candidate library is pyatv, assessed from its streaming guide, its interface API, the 0.18.0 source, and a prototype backend driven against two real receivers.

Python 3.14. pyatv 0.18.0 (June 2026) declares 3.14. Its native dependency miniaudio ships cp314 manylinux wheels and the rest are pure Python. It adds six packages (chacha20poly1305-reuseable, miniaudio, pyatv, srptools, tabulate, tinytag).

Two playback paths.

stream.play_url(url) (AirPlay) stream.stream_file(src) (RAOP) Who fetches audio the receiver fetches the URL pyatv fetches/decodes, then pushes ALAC over RTP Receivers AirPlay video receivers only (Apple TV class) AirPort Express, HomePod, AirPlay speakers, Apple TV Formats what the receiver decodes MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG decoded by miniaudio Wire format original bytes ALAC at the receiver's mDNS sr/ss/ch, by default 44.1 kHz/16-bit/2 ch Control stop only (pause/seek need MRP on Apple TV) stop, volume, metadata; "pause" = stop Returns when playback ends (request held open) when the stream ends

play_url is only offered when the receiver advertises an AirPlay video feature flag (SupportsAirPlayVideoV1/V2); audio-only receivers never get it. AirPlay 2 receivers that set HasUnifiedAdvertiserInfo take RAOP through the AirPlay service, so the absence of a separate _raop._tcp record does not mean "URL playback only".

Pairing. tvOS ≥ 10.2 and most AirPlay 2 receivers require device authentication. pyatv.pair() → begin() / pin() / finish() yields a credentials string that must be stored and passed back on every connect; HomePods and some third-party receivers use transient pairing, which pyatv does by itself without a PIN.

Timing. pyatv says playback starts about 2 s after streaming begins, from receiver buffering it cannot shorten, and the receiver gives "no feedback if anything is not working". pyatv has no PTP clock, so it cannot do AirPlay 2 multiroom sync.

Seeking. RAOP streams from the start; pyatv's RAOP pause() stops the stream. play_url accepts a start position but has no mid-stream seek without MRP.

Gapless. Each stream_file call is one RTSP session (SETUP → RECORD → TEARDOWN). Track N+1 starts a new session with the ~2 s buffer, so gapless playback is not achievable per track. Only a continuous stream could be gapless (ADR-0010).

docs.title: Hardware evaluation (2026-10-29)
docs.text:
A prototype backend (pyatv 0.18.0) was run against two AirPlay 2 receivers: an audio streamer that advertises RAOP and a TV that advertises AirPlay only.

Naim Uniti Atom (AirPlay 2, firmware 3.11, AirTunes/366.0): nothing played.

  • With srptools 2.0.0 (released 2026-10-26, three days earlier) every connection failed inside pyatv: SRPClientSession.__init__() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given. srptools 2.0 made the private key keyword-only; pyatv 0.18 passes it positionally. Any pyatv user needs srptools<2 until pyatv is fixed. This breaks all authentication and pairing, not just this receiver.
  • With srptools pinned to 1.0.1, pyatv's AirPlay 2 RAOP session reached SETUP, but the receiver answered the text-metadata SET_PARAMETER (application/x-dmap-tagged) with 500, which aborts the stream. Initial volume SET_PARAMETERs also got 500 (pyatv retries those).
  • With text metadata suppressed, RECORD/FLUSH succeeded, but the audio UDP port refused the packets (Connection refused) within a second.
  • Forcing AirPlay 1 (protocol_version = 1): the connection dropped after ANNOUNCE.

Sony XR-65X90J TV (AirPlay 2, AirTunes/377.40.00, pairing Mandatory):

  • No video feature flag, so play_url is unavailable ("play_url is not supported"). Choosing the playback path from whether a separate RAOP service exists, as the prototype did, picks the one path this TV can never use.
  • Through RAOP on the unified AirPlay service, pyatv paired transiently without a PIN and the TV played the stream.
  • pyatv sent volume: -20.1 (its 33 % default) at stream start, replacing the TV's own volume. The test track played very loud. Every stream start does this unless the caller passes a volume explicitly.
  • Volume changes made with the TV remote arrived as pyatv events (POST /command on the event channel); the prototype ignored them.

Prototype behaviour that was wrong on real hardware:

  • It reported PLAYING once a stream survived 3 s without failing. On the Naim the stream died about 10 s in, so it showed PLAYING while nothing played: the false PLAYING that #316's first priority removed elsewhere.
  • pyatv's HTTP source waits its full 10 s read timeout at end of file while reading tags, which delays start.
  • Resume restarted the track; track completion was never observed, because no track reached its end.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
No AirPlay backend ships. The airplay renderer kind stays reserved; the prototype, its migration, API, web pairing UI and the pyatv dependency were removed before merge.

pyatv 0.18 cannot stream to one of the two receivers tested at all, needs a dependency pin to work at all, and overrides the receiver's volume on every stream start. A backend built on it would need, at minimum, before being offered:

  • srptools<2 (or a pyatv release that supports srptools 2);
  • the playback path chosen from the feature flags (unified RAOP over the AirPlay service), never from the presence of a separate RAOP record;
  • no volume sent unless the user changed it in Jamarr, and receiver-side volume changes followed from pyatv's events;
  • PLAYING reported from receiver feedback, not from a timer;
  • text metadata skipped for receivers that refuse it, without failing the stream;
  • testing on each receiver family at an agreed time and volume.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Jamarr cannot play to AirPlay receivers. Both receivers tested also speak UPnP AVTransport (and the TV Cast), which Jamarr supports.
  • Revisit when pyatv supports srptools 2 and AirPlay 2 audio more completely, or if an AirPlay-only receiver becomes important. The hardware notes above are the starting test plan.
  • A continuous-stream mode (ADR-0010) would still be the only route to gapless AirPlay.

docs.title: ADR-0008: Fire TV: no Fling; Matter Casting not viable for a server today
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed (evaluation; no implementation)
  • Date: 2026-10-28 (#316, Priority 3)

docs.title: 316 asks whether modern Fire TV support is worth adding. Requirements:
docs.text:
URL loading, metadata, serialized control commands and status callbacks behind an explicit capability-aware adapter, with no new Amazon Fling dependency.

  • Fling: Amazon ended standard support for the Fling SDK on 2026-03-05 and directs new work to Matter Casting. Its integration page now returns 404. Fling is ruled out.
  • Matter Casting, from Amazon's overview and integration guide and the connectedhomeip examples/tv-casting-app. It has three roles:
    • Player: Fire TV (Fire OS 7+) or Echo Show.
    • Content app: an app installed on the Fire TV that declares Matter clusters (Content Launcher, Media Playback, Account Login, …) and receives MATTER_COMMAND intents through Amazon's Matter agent. Its manifest carries a vendor ID and product ID.
    • Casting client: Amazon documents only Android/iOS SDKs. The connectedhomeip repo has a C++ Linux sample client.
  • Onboarding is User Directed Commissioning (UDC). The client joins the player's Matter fabric with an 8-digit passcode shown on the TV, once per player. The client must present a Device Attestation Certificate, and Amazon says production needs a valid DAC. In practice that means a CSA vendor ID and attestation chain, not the test vendor 0xFFF1 (65521) used in the examples.
  • Casting drives a content app. Neither page says the player can play a bare URL without a cooperating app on the TV.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Do not build a Fire TV backend now.

  1. Server-side Matter Casting client: not viable. Python has no maintained binding for the casting client. The Linux path is a C++ sample built inside the connectedhomeip tree. Production attestation needs a DAC chain that a self-hosted, open-source server cannot ship credibly. And it would still need a Jamarr content app on the TV to play anything.
  2. What an adapter would need, if revisited:
    • a Jamarr content app on Fire TV. The Android client is the natural base, but it has no Android TV/leanback manifest today. It would implement Content Launcher (LaunchURL/LaunchContent to a Jamarr track or queue), Media Playback (play/pause/seek/stop plus state attributes) and Account Login.
    • a casting client holding fabric credentials and a DAC.
    • a backend mapping those clusters onto RendererBackend and SupportsStatusEvents, with pairing: required (the UDC passcode).
  3. Pragmatic alternative: a Fire TV can already sideload the Jamarr Android app and play locally. If server-driven control of such a device is wanted, the cheaper design is a Jamarr-native "remote client" renderer: the app registers with the server and takes commands over the existing authenticated channel. No Matter fabric, DAC or vendor registration is needed. That is a separate feature, not a Matter adapter.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No Fling or Matter dependency is added. Fire TV owners use the Android app directly. If Amazon's DLNA/Cast apps are installed, they cover UPnP/Cast as any renderer.
  • Unverified:
    • whether current Fire OS builds accept a third-party casting client with a development DAC
    • whether a Fire TV can play a URL with no content app
    • the Linux sample's state None of these were tested; no Fire TV was used.
  • Revisit if the CSA/Amazon publish a server or desktop casting SDK with practical attestation, or if Jamarr gains an Android TV build.

docs.title: ADR-0009: DLNA server and renderer-bridge roles: arbitration first, then scope
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed (design; no implementation)
  • Date: 2026-10-28 (#316, Priority 3)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Today Jamarr is only a UPnP control point: it discovers renderers and drives them. #316 raises two more roles.

  1. Media Server (ContentDirectory + ConnectionManager). Browse-only TVs and players could pull music from Jamarr: browse/search, artwork, permissions and resource serving.
  2. Renderer / bridge facade. Jamarr would expose Jamarr-managed playback devices (Cast, AirPlay, local) as UPnP MediaRenderers or OpenHome devices, so third-party control points (BubbleUPnP, Linn Kazoo, …) could drive them.

A separate item is a standalone Android Cast path without Play Services.

The hard part of the bridge is not SOAP. Once Jamarr's own clients and a third-party controller both drive one device, two questions need answers: who owns the queue, and whose command wins.

docs.title: Queue ownership for a facade
docs.text:
Use the ADR-0006 vocabulary:

  • AVTransport facade → server-owned queue. A third-party controller sends SetAVTransportURI / SetNextAVTransportURI with its own URIs, often from another media server. The facade treats that as a foreign session. Jamarr's queue for the device is suspended, not overwritten. Jamarr plays the foreign URI through the device backend and reports transport state back. SetNext maps to the backend's SupportsNextTrackStaging where present, and to a one-slot server queue elsewhere. History/scrobbling apply only when the URI resolves to a Jamarr track.
  • OpenHome facade → renderer-owned queue. Playlist Insert / DeleteId / ReadList / SeekId edit the Jamarr queue for that device directly. The queue becomes shared, so Jamarr clients and Kazoo see one playlist. The facade advertises queue_ownership: renderer to controllers while the underlying device stays server-driven.

docs.title: Control arbitration
docs.text:
• One owner per device at a time, recorded with the renderer state: the jamarr session or a foreign:<controller-ip> session.
  • Last writer wins for transport commands (play, pause, stop, seek, volume). Both sides see the change through status events: GENA LastChange for UPnP controllers, the existing state polling/SSE for Jamarr clients.
  • Queue replacement needs ownership. A Jamarr client loading a new queue while a foreign session is active takes ownership back and stops the foreign URI. A foreign SetAVTransportURI does the reverse.
  • Volume is device state, not session state, and is shared.
  • The facade never answers SetNextAVTransportURI for devices that cannot honour it. Capabilities stay truthful to the facade too.

docs.title: Scope order
docs.text:
1. Media Server first. It is read-only and touches no playback state. It reuses existing library queries, artwork and /api/stream. It needs DIDL-Lite generation, an SSDP advertiser (today Jamarr only searches) and an access model: UPnP has no auth, so per-user permissions become LAN-trust plus a configurable "DLNA library user" whose stream tokens the server mints. It stays opt-in and off by default.
  2. OpenHome facade after a native OpenHome backend exists (ADR-0011, not built) and settles the Playlist ID mapping, since the facade mirrors it.
  3. AVTransport facade last. Its foreign-session model is the most intrusive change to the orchestrator.

docs.title: Android Cast without Play Services
docs.text: Recorded as a separate feature. The server keeps pychromecast and does not replace its protocol implementation. Device-direct Cast on de-Googled Android (ADR-0004) would need a CASTV2 client in Kotlin (TLS, protobuf, device auth) without the Cast SDK. It is substantial and independent of the bridge roles.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Nothing ships now. The ownership/arbitration model above is the precondition for any facade work.
  • A Media Server makes the library readable by any LAN device, so it must stay opt-in.
  • Unverified: controller behaviour (BubbleUPnP, Kazoo, TV built-in players) against a Jamarr facade, and DLNA profile requirements of specific TVs. No implementation or hardware test exists.

docs.title: ADR-0010: Continuous-stream mode for seamless album playback on Cast
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed (evaluation; no implementation)
  • Date: 2026-10-28 (#316, Priority 2: Cast queues/preloading)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Server Cast loads one track per LOAD. Each transition goes IDLE(FINISHED), then the next LOAD, then the receiver buffers, so live albums and classical works get audible gaps. #316 asks to evaluate two remedies:

  • Receiver queues and preloading (QUEUE_LOAD / QUEUE_INSERT, preloadTime). This is being implemented separately in the Cast session/queue work. This ADR does not repeat it. A receiver queue preloads the next item, but does not by itself prove gapless playback: the Default Media Receiver may still tear down and re-create its decoder between items.
  • A continuous PCM/audio stream: one long HTTP response that concatenates the tracks. The device sees one endless media item, so transitions happen inside Jamarr's encoder and can be sample-accurate.

docs.title: Evaluation of continuous-stream mode
docs.text: Concern Effect Gapless Best possible: Jamarr decodes track N and N+1 into one PCM timeline. Encoder delay/padding is handled once, not per track. Seeking Receiver-side seek is lost or wrong. A live stream (streamType: LIVE, no Content-Length) is not seekable. A "seek" becomes stop and reload the stream at a new offset, which costs a full rebuffer. Within-track seek is server-driven. Metadata The receiver shows the first item's metadata. Per-track title/art needs Jamarr to push metadata updates. The Default Media Receiver does not reliably honour mid-stream updates; ICY metadata is not supported. In practice it needs a custom receiver, or accepting album-level metadata. Position / progress The receiver reports position in the stream timeline. Jamarr must map it back to (track, offset) and drive history/scrobbling from that mapping, not from receiver IDLE events. Buffering Receivers buffer ahead (several seconds or more). Queue edits, skips and pause are only audible after the buffered audio drains, so "skip" means reloading the stream. Pausing a live stream may make the receiver drop it after a timeout. Cancellation The encoder must stop when the receiver disconnects, and a reload must cancel the old pipeline. That requires one ffmpeg/encoder process per active session, with a hard owner and teardown. Today's cached, seekable transcodes cannot be reused. Format WAV/LPCM over HTTP has no length for an endless stream. FLAC (streamable, no seektable) or a lossless-compressed live stream fits better. The output must satisfy the device constraints the audio planner knows (OutputConstraints). Tokens One stream token must live for the whole session. That makes the open revocation question (ADR-0003) more pressing.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Do not make continuous streaming the default for Cast. The receiver-queue work comes first. Then measure transition silence on real receivers before deciding whether continuous mode is needed at all.
  • If measurement shows audible gaps with receiver queues, add continuous mode as an opt-in per-renderer mode for "seamless album" playback. It reports queue_ownership: continuous_stream (ADR-0006), with can_seek: false (server-side reload instead) and server-pushed metadata. The UI shares queue concepts with server-owned queues.
  • The same mode is the only route to gapless playback on AirPlay/RAOP (ADR-0007), where each track is otherwise a separate RTSP session.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No code yet. The cost is a long-lived encoder per session, a stream-timeline mapping for history, and degraded seek/skip latency.
  • Unverified:
    • transition silence with and without receiver queues
    • Default Media Receiver behaviour with endless FLAC/LPCM streams
    • how the receiver handles pause on a live stream
    • whether mid-stream metadata updates display None have been measured on hardware.

docs.title: ADR-0011: Native OpenHome/Linn backend — evaluated, not built
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted (evaluation; no backend ships)
  • Date: 2026-10-29 (#316, Priority 3)

docs.title: 316 asks to evaluate a native OpenHome/Linn backend: Product / Playlist / Time
docs.text:
/ Volume / Info and the legacy Linn variants as separate capabilities; Jamarr tracks mapped to renderer queue ids (Insert / ReadList / DeleteId / SeekId); device-side shuffle/repeat; event-based reconciliation; several controllers agreeing on one renderer-owned playlist; source/standby only where supported; and never assuming AVTransport.

A prototype was written from the OpenHome service specifications and the legacy Linn SCPDs, and tested only against in-memory fakes. A network scan on 2026-10-29 (SSDP ssdp:all plus each description's service list) found no device advertising any av-openhome-org or linn-co-uk service; every renderer present is plain AVTransport. Nothing could be tested on hardware, so the prototype was removed before merge.

docs.title: What the prototype established
docs.text:
OpenHome is a different queue model. The device holds the whole playlist, advances through it by itself, and other controllers (Kazoo, BubbleUPnP, …) edit the same list. Jamarr would mirror it, not load one track at a time: queue_ownership: renderer in the capability contract (ADR-0006).

Detection, per service and per action. Search urn:av-openhome-org:service:Playlist:1 in addition to the AVTransport targets. Classify every service separately (av-openhome-org Product / Playlist / Time / Volume / Info / Radio / Transport; legacy linn-co-uk Ds / Playlist / Preamp / Product / Time / Info) and every operation against the actions in its SCPD. Nothing implies anything else: a Playlist does not imply Volume or Product, Product without SetStandby gives no standby, and OpenHome never implies AVTransport. Queue operations come from one family (OpenHome Playlist, or Linn Playlist + Ds), because item ids are only valid within the service that issued them. Bind arguments positionally to the SCPD's own names, so OpenHome (AfterId) and Linn (aAfterId) take the same call.

Routing. A device with both OpenHome and AVTransport should prefer OpenHome, also when one description holds exactly one OpenHome Source and one plain MediaRenderer as sibling devices, with a per-device override to stay on AVTransport. An OpenHome-only device is only playable this way.

Queue mapping.

Jamarr action Device set queue DeleteAll; insert the start track, SeekId + Play; insert the rest around it (capped at TracksMax) in the background append / reorder / remove minimal edit: ids already in order stay (the playing one always), others DeleteId + Insert; non-Jamarr entries never touched skip / play track SeekId (inserting first if needed) pause / resume / stop / seek Pause / Play / Stop / SeekSecondAbsolute, on the active source's Transport (or Radio) when another source is selected volume / mute Volume (or Preamp) SetVolume scaled to VolumeMax, SetMute clear DeleteAll before playing leave standby and select the Playlist source, only if Product has those actions

Each Jamarr queue item stores the renderer-assigned id. Queue edits must hold a per-renderer lock from the stored write until the device has the edit, or a reconciliation in the gap rebuilds the queue from the device and drops the new items.

Formats. The Playlist's own ProtocolInfo (legacy Ds.ProtocolInfo) says what the queue accepts, in the same shape as ConnectionManager GetProtocolInfo, so the protocolInfo negotiation and playback plan that AVTransport uses apply unchanged. Insert has no metadata stages to fall back through.

Stream tokens. The device fetches each URL whenever it gets there, possibly days later. Tokens must cover the wait plus playback, capped (7 days was the prototype's default), and items still queued whose token nears expiry must be swapped in place (Insert the fresh copy after the old id, then DeleteId), never touching the playing item.

Events. Playlist (IdArray, Id, TransportState, Shuffle, Repeat), Time and Volume, or their Linn equivalents, plus Product, Info, Radio and Transport where present, subscribed through the same GENA manager as AVTransport (app/services/upnp/events.py): one NOTIFY server, shared renewal, backoff and health. Healthy only when Playlist, Time and Volume all are; otherwise poll, bounded (2 s while playing, 15 s otherwise). The IdArray is the queue: ids another controller inserted are resolved with ReadList, and ones pointing at /api/stream/<id> become Jamarr tracks. The current Id becomes current_index, and history runs off it once per play. Jamarr never advances the queue itself.

Other sources. Product SourceIndex/SourceXml say which source is active. While it is not the Playlist (radio, an input, a streaming service), transport controls go to that source's Transport (or Radio) service, and Info describes what plays.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: No OpenHome backend ships. With no OpenHome device available, the prototype could only be checked against fakes written from the same reading of the specification, which proves nothing about real firmware. The design above is the starting point if one is built.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• OpenHome-only renderers are not offered. Devices that also speak AVTransport play through the UPnP backend, without device-side shuffle/repeat/standby/source or a shared multi-controller playlist.
  • The capability contract keeps queue_ownership / queue_operations (ADR-0006), so a renderer-owned backend can be added without changing the API.
  • To build it, test against a real device first. Without Linn hardware, upmpdcli (a software OpenHome renderer on MPD) is a practical test device, though not a substitute for Linn firmware.
  • The OpenHome bridge facade in ADR-0009 depends on this backend existing.

docs.title: Native Android and Android Auto Approach
Goal
docs.text:
Add a native Android client for Jamarr without turning the backend into a new platform project.

The Android app should be another Jamarr client. It should reuse the existing FastAPI API, auth model, stream URL flow, artwork endpoints, and library data as much as possible. Android Auto support should play through Android's MediaSession in the car; it should not use Jamarr's UPnP renderer support.

This document intentionally separates the first safe milestone from optional later improvements. The first milestone should be small enough to validate the approach before committing to larger API work.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• No rewrite of the current web API.
  • No changes to the Svelte UI contract unless independently needed.
  • No Android Auto support for UPnP renderers.
  • No new backend queue system for Android in the first milestone.
  • No new auth model in the first milestone.
  • No database schema changes in the first milestone.
  • No broad /api/mobile platform redesign before a working Android prototype proves what is actually needed.

docs.title: Sequence Plan
docs.text: The work should be staged so each step proves one thing and keeps backend risk low. Stages 0-2 are the real initial scope. Later stages are optional and should only happen after the earlier stages expose a concrete need.

docs.title: Stage 0: API Survey
docs.text:
Goal: confirm which existing Jamarr endpoints the Android app can already use.

Work:

  1. List the current auth, search, library, artwork, and stream URL endpoints.
  2. Identify the smallest path from "logged in" to "play one track".
  3. Note missing fields only if they block Android playback.

Backend changes allowed: none.

Exit criteria:

  • A short endpoint map exists for the Android prototype.
  • There is a known existing endpoint path to find or select a track.
  • There is a known existing endpoint path to generate a playable stream URL.

Stage 0 output: API Reference.

docs.title: Stage 1: Phone Playback Prototype
docs.text:
Goal: prove native Android can play Jamarr audio without backend redesign.

Work:

  1. Create the native Android project.
  2. Store a Jamarr server URL.
  3. Log in using the existing auth endpoints.
  4. Fetch enough library or search data to select one track.
  5. Request an existing Jamarr stream URL for that track.
  6. Play the stream with Android Media3/ExoPlayer.

Backend changes allowed: none unless a tiny compatibility fix is required to play one track.

Exit criteria:

  • The app can log in.
  • The app can select one Jamarr track.
  • The app can play that track through ExoPlayer.
  • The web UI still works without changes.

docs.title: Stage 2: MediaSession Foundation
docs.text:
Goal: make Android own playback in the standard Android way.

Work:

  1. Add a Media3 MediaSession.
  2. Connect ExoPlayer to the session.
  3. Show Android media notification controls.
  4. Support play, pause, seek, previous, and next inside the phone app.

Backend changes allowed: none.

Exit criteria:

  • Lock screen and notification controls work.
  • Headset/media button controls work.
  • Playback state is reported by Android's MediaSession, not Jamarr's UPnP renderer state.

docs.title: Stage 3: Android Auto Browse Prototype
docs.text:
Goal: prove Android Auto can browse and play Jamarr tracks through the phone's media session.

Work:

  1. Add a Media3 MediaLibraryService.
  2. Expose a small Android Auto browse tree.
  3. Map browse selections to Jamarr track IDs.
  4. Resolve selected tracks to existing Jamarr stream URLs.
  5. Test with Android Auto Desktop Head Unit or a real car.

Backend changes allowed: none at first. If current web-shaped endpoints make the media tree awkward, stop and add the small adapter described in the next stage.

Exit criteria:

  • Android Auto can display at least one browse path.
  • Android Auto can start playback.
  • Playback happens through ExoPlayer and MediaSession.
  • No UPnP or Jamarr renderer state is involved.

docs.title: Stage 4: Minimal Android Adapter, Only If Needed
docs.text:
Goal: reduce Android Auto client complexity if the existing API is awkward for tree-shaped browsing.

Work:

  1. Add one narrow FastAPI router at app/api/android.py.
  2. Add only these routes:
  3. GET /api/android/browse/root
  4. GET /api/android/browse/{node_id}/children
  5. POST /api/android/resolve
  6. Reuse existing auth and existing database/library/stream logic.
  7. Add focused tests for the new routes.

Backend changes allowed: one additive router only. No migrations, no web route changes, no auth rewrite, no player rewrite.

Exit criteria:

  • Android Auto browse code is simpler than it was against the web API.
  • Existing web UI behavior is unchanged.
  • New tests cover the adapter routes.

docs.title: Stage 5: Phone UI Expansion
docs.text:
Goal: turn the prototype into a useful phone app.

Work:

  1. Add basic library screens.
  2. Add search.
  3. Add artist, album, and playlist detail screens.
  4. Add now-playing and queue UI managed locally by Android Media3.

Backend changes allowed: small additive fields or endpoint fixes only when the Android UI proves a specific gap.

Exit criteria:

  • The phone app can browse enough of the library to be useful.
  • Local Android playback remains independent of Jamarr UPnP playback.

docs.title: Stage 6: Optional Hardening
docs.text:
Goal: improve reliability and polish after the core app works.

Possible work:

  • Android playback history reporting.
  • Better artwork sizing or caching.
  • Batch stream URL resolution.
  • Offline downloads.
  • Android device/session management.
  • Mobile-specific queue persistence.

Backend changes allowed: only individually justified additions. Avoid grouping these into one large platform rewrite.

Exit criteria:

  • Each hardening item has a concrete problem it solves.
  • Each item can be tested independently.

docs.title: First Milestone Summary
docs.text:
The first real milestone is the end of Stage 2: Android can log in, play one Jamarr track with ExoPlayer, and expose that playback through Media3 MediaSession.

Android Auto begins in Stage 3. The optional /api/android backend adapter is Stage 4, not a prerequisite.

docs.title: Android App Shape
docs.text:
Use a normal native Android app:

  • Kotlin
  • Jetpack Compose for phone UI
  • Media3 ExoPlayer for playback
  • Media3 Session for MediaSession / Android Auto integration
  • Retrofit or Ktor for HTTP
  • DataStore for server URL and local app preferences
  • Secure local storage for refresh/session material

Suggested package layout:

android/
  app/
    ui/          # Compose screens
    data/        # Jamarr API client and DTOs
    auth/        # Login, refresh, token storage
    playback/    # ExoPlayer and MediaSession
    car/         # MediaLibraryService for Android Auto

The first app does not need a full Jamarr UI. A small login screen, search or library picker, and now-playing screen are enough to validate the playback path.

docs.title: Android Auto Model
docs.text:
Android Auto media apps are not custom projected phone screens. The car host connects to the app's media service, asks for a browsable media tree, and sends playback commands through the app's media session.

For Jamarr, Android Auto should be:

Jamarr FastAPI -> Android app -> ExoPlayer -> MediaSession -> Android Auto

It should not be:

Android Auto -> Jamarr backend player state -> UPnP renderer

The app owns playback in the car. Jamarr provides metadata, artwork, and stream URLs.

docs.title: Backend Strategy
docs.text:
Start with no backend changes. If Android Auto needs a cleaner browse tree than the current web API naturally provides, add one narrow adapter router.

The adapter should:

  • live under new Android-specific paths;
  • reuse existing auth dependencies;
  • use existing database/library query logic where practical;
  • avoid schema changes;
  • avoid changing existing web endpoints;
  • return a small Android-friendly media item shape.

Suggested file if needed:

app/api/android.py

Suggested route prefix if needed:

/api/android

docs.title: Minimal Optional Android Adapter
docs.text: Only add this after the first Android playback prototype works and the Android Auto MediaLibraryService proves that current endpoints are awkward.

docs.title: GET /api/android/browse/root
docs.text:
Returns a small fixed set of top-level folders for Android Auto.

Example:

{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "recent",
      "title": "Recently Played",
      "browsable": true,
      "playable": false
    },
    {
      "id": "playlists",
      "title": "Playlists",
      "browsable": true,
      "playable": false
    },
    {
      "id": "artists",
      "title": "Artists",
      "browsable": true,
      "playable": false
    },
    {
      "id": "albums",
      "title": "Albums",
      "browsable": true,
      "playable": false
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: GET /api/android/browse/{node_id}/children
docs.text:
Maps simple node IDs to existing Jamarr data.

Possible mappings:

recent           -> recent tracks or playback history
playlists        -> playlist list
playlist:{id}    -> playlist tracks
artists          -> artist list
artist:{mbid}    -> artist albums or tracks
albums           -> album list
album:{id}       -> album tracks

Response shape:

{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "track:123",
      "title": "Dreams",
      "subtitle": "Fleetwood Mac",
      "image_url": "/api/art/...",
      "browsable": false,
      "playable": true
    }
  ]
}

The Android app should treat id as opaque. The backend can parse IDs however it wants internally.

docs.title: POST /api/android/resolve
docs.text:
Converts an Android media item ID into a playable stream.

Request:

{
  "id": "track:123"
}

Response:

{
  "id": "track:123",
  "track_id": 123,
  "stream_url": "/api/stream/123?token=...",
  "title": "Dreams",
  "artist": "Fleetwood Mac",
  "album": "Rumours",
  "duration_ms": 257000,
  "image_url": "/api/art/..."
}

This should wrap the existing Jamarr stream URL behavior. It should not create a new streaming system.

docs.title: Why This Adapter Is Small
docs.text:
The adapter is not a new API platform. It is a translation layer between:

  • Android Auto's tree-shaped media browsing model; and
  • Jamarr's existing library, playlist, history, artwork, and stream data.

It should be read-only except for stream URL generation, which Jamarr already does. It should not own playback state.

docs.title: What To Defer
docs.text:
These may be useful later, but they should not block the first app:

  • Android-specific playback history reporting.
  • Offline downloads.
  • Batch stream URL resolution.
  • Artwork resizing/caching endpoints.
  • Android session/device management.
  • Mobile-specific queue persistence.
  • A generalized /api/mobile/v1 API.
  • Car App Library templated media screens.

Add these only after the first Android app shows a concrete need.

docs.title: Risk Controls
docs.text:
• Keep all new backend routes under /api/android.
  • Do not modify existing web routes for Android.
  • Add focused tests only for any new Android adapter endpoints.
  • Avoid migrations for the first Android work.
  • Keep Android Auto playback local to Android Media3.
  • Use the existing Jamarr stream URL endpoint for actual file access.

docs.title: Main Decision
docs.text:
The important decision is to prove playback before designing a larger API. If the proof of concept can play Jamarr tracks through Media3, Android Auto support becomes a focused media-service task rather than a backend rewrite.

The order is:

  1. API survey.
  2. Phone playback prototype.
  3. MediaSession foundation.
  4. Android Auto browse prototype.
  5. Minimal Android adapter only if needed.
  6. Phone UI expansion.
  7. Optional hardening.

docs.title: Stage 3 Plan: Android Auto v1 - 2026-04-25
docs.text:
Stages 0-2 are complete. Stage 5 (Phone UI) is well past its original scope: home, search, artist detail, album detail, playlists, charts, history, favourites, queue/now playing, and history+scrobble reporting all ship in the phone app. The next milestone is in-car playback through Android Auto.

This section captures the concrete decisions made before any car-related code. Stage 4's /api/android adapter is not part of v1 - existing endpoints map to the planned browse tree without change.

docs.title: Auth in the car
docs.text:
The car has no UI for typing a password. The MediaLibraryService runs on the phone and reuses the access token already in DataStore.

  • If the token is missing or expired beyond refresh, the root browse tree returns a single non-playable item titled "Sign in on phone to use Jamarr".
  • The existing JamarrApiClient auth interceptor handles refresh transparently while the car session is live.
  • No in-car login flow.

docs.title: Service architecture
docs.text: Upgrade the existing JamarrPlaybackService extends MediaSessionService to extend MediaLibraryService instead. MediaLibraryService is a subclass of MediaSessionService, so the phone behaviour is preserved and the same service serves both phone and car. No second service.

docs.title: Browse tree
docs.text:
Drive-safe and shallow. The artist and album catalogues are too large to be useful as flat lists in the car, so they are intentionally not root nodes - voice/text search is the entry point for "play ". 

Root
├── Favourites
│   ├── Artists  → artist   → albums   → tracks
│   └── Releases → album    → tracks
└── Playlists    → playlist → tracks
├── Recently PLayed
│   ├── Albums   → album    → tracks
├── Charts
│   ├── Albums   → album    → tracks
├── History
│   ├── Albums   → album    → tracks
│   └── Artists  → artist   → albums   → tracks
├── Recently Added
│   ├── Albums   → album    → tracks

Tap behaviour:

  • Track: play it; queue siblings (album/playlist) for prev/next.
  • Album / playlist: play from track 1.
  • Artist: show albums (no auto-play; "Shuffle artist" deferred).

Search is wired through MediaLibrarySession.Callback.onSearch later (see deferred section). For v1, AA's text search field will be empty.

docs.title: Stream URL lifecycle
docs.text:
Stream URLs are short-lived, signed tokens. The current phone code resolves the whole queue's URLs up front, which would fail mid-drive on long playlists.

For Android Auto - and the phone, since they share the service - switch to lazy resolution: implement a Media3 ResolvingDataSource.Factory that calls GET /api/stream-url/{id} immediately before each track plays. The MediaItem holds the track id; the data source resolves it to a fresh URL on demand.

No backend change. This also fixes any "queue dies after N tracks" issue from expired tokens.

docs.title: Artwork
docs.text:
MediaMetadata.artworkUri is fetched by the AA system process, not by our app, so it can't carry our bearer token. v1 embeds bytes:

  • Fetch artwork via OkHttp/Coil using the existing /api/art/file/{sha1}?max_size=400 endpoint (auth header attached as normal).
  • Set the bytes on MediaMetadata.artworkData.
  • ~30-100 KB per track in the session bundle - acceptable for now.

If memory/IPC cost becomes a problem, revisit with a signed art URL endpoint.

docs.title: History reporting and Last.fm scrobbling
docs.text:
These ship in v1 (not deferred). The phone already calls POST /api/player/queue, POST /api/player/index, and POST /api/player/progress from the polling loop in JamarrApp.kt. The same loop must keep running while AA is connected; nothing about car playback should disable it.

The polling loop is driven by MediaController state, not by the foreground UI, so it should continue working when the phone screen is off and AA is in control. Verify this explicitly during DHU testing - history rows for in-car playback must appear at the same 30s/20% threshold the web UI uses.

docs.title: Manifest and discovery
docs.text:
• Add res/xml/automotive_app_desc.xml:
<automotiveApp>
    <uses name="media"/>
</automotiveApp>
  • Application-level meta-data:
<meta-data
    android:name="com.google.android.gms.car.application"
    android:resource="@xml/automotive_app_desc"/>
  • The service intent filter keeps MediaSessionService and adds MediaLibraryService (Media3 dispatches to both).

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Use Android Studio's Desktop Head Unit (DHU) to iterate without driving:

  • Install DHU via the SDK Manager (Extras > Android Auto Desktop Head Unit).
  • Phone needs USB debugging + AA developer mode enabled.
  • A small helper script under android/scripts/dhu.sh should:
  • check adb is available,
  • start the phone-side AA in head-unit-server mode,
  • launch the DHU binary,
  • tear everything down on Ctrl-C.

The android/README.md (or root README) needs a "Testing in the car" section linking to the script and noting prerequisites. Real-car validation is the final step.

docs.title: Deferred to v2
docs.text:
• Voice/text search (onSearch) - intentional v1 omission.
  • Custom session commands (favourite from car, etc.).
  • Offline downloads.
  • Pagination/alphabet scaffolding for full Artists/Albums browse - rejected for v1; search covers the use case.
  • The /api/android adapter - revisit only if a v1 awkwardness justifies it.

docs.title: Implementation order
docs.text:
1. Lazy stream resolution via ResolvingDataSource.Factory (fixes phone bug too).
  2. Service upgrade to MediaLibraryService + manifest changes.
  3. Root browse tree + Recently Played + Favourites + Playlists nodes.
  4. Drilldown nodes (album→tracks, artist→albums, playlist→tracks).
  5. Embedded artwork on MediaMetadata.
  6. DHU helper script + README.
  7. Verify history/scrobble reporting still works under AA.

docs.title: Stage 1 Result
docs.text:
Stage 1 is complete for the POC.

Implementation details:

  • Login sends the existing JSON body:
{
  "username": "your_username",

Installed on 1 device.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
These are acceptable for the current POC but should be addressed later:

  • Access tokens are stored in DataStore. Refresh-cookie/session handling is not fully implemented yet.
  • Refresh/session material is not stored in encrypted storage yet.
  • Stream URLs are resolved eagerly for a whole queue. Later, resolve URLs lazily when a track is about to play so short-lived stream tokens do not expire in a long queue.
  • Album playback currently fetches album tracks from the existing web-shaped /api/tracks route.
  • Artist cards do not open artist detail screens yet; they trigger a search.
  • No playlist, album detail, artist detail, or full library screens yet.
  • No playback history reporting from Android yet.
  • No Android Auto MediaLibraryService browse tree yet. That remains Stage 3.
  • No /api/android adapter exists. Stage 4 should only be added if Android Auto browsing proves the current API is too awkward.

docs.title: Android Auto Hardening - 2026-08-11
docs.text: Stage 3 shipped a working browse tree; this pass fixed the behaviour that only shows up in a car, and added the test stack to keep it fixed.

docs.title: Browse tree
docs.text:
• Paging is honoured. Media3 forwards EXTRA_PAGE/EXTRA_PAGE_SIZE from legacy browsers and only falls back to (0, MAX_VALUE) when the browser sends no options. Nodes now build a light row list, apply the window, and turn only that page into MediaItems.
  • Failures are errors. A node that cannot load returns LibraryResult.ofError (ERROR_SESSION_AUTHENTICATION_EXPIRED for 401/403, ERROR_IO otherwise) instead of an empty list that reads as an empty library.
  • Sign-in refreshes the tree. notifyChildrenChanged fires for every static node when the stored session changes, so the car stops showing "Sign in on phone" without a reconnect.
  • Every static node resolves via onGetItem, not just root's children, so a restored browse stack does not fail.
  • Entries with no MBID are dropped rather than offered as browsable folders that open empty.
  • Album, playlist, Singles and Most Scrobbled folders lead with "Play all".
  • Subtitles come with displayTitle. Media3 only forwards subtitle when displayTitle is set; otherwise it derives the description from MediaMetadataCompat.PREFERRED_DESCRIPTION_ORDER and drops it.
  • Track items carry durationMs, artist and album.

docs.title: Playback
docs.text:
• onAddMediaItems resolves only. Sibling expansion belongs to onSetMediaItems — "add to queue" of one track must add one track.
  • Queue expansion no longer fetches artwork: nothing renders queue items, and every fetch delayed the first note. The artwork URI is still set.
  • Voice search is still unimplemented. The manifest must advertise MEDIA_PLAY_FROM_SEARCH (lint MissingIntentFilterForMediaSearch fails the build without it for a media Auto app), so a search request is now rejected with an error rather than handed to the player as an item with no URI.
  • Playback resumption works: the last queue is written to DataStore and restored from onPlaybackResumption, with androidx.media3.session.MediaButtonReceiver declared so the system media button reaches the service.

docs.title: Artwork
docs.text:
The Stage 3 note that artworkUri "can't carry our bearer token" does not apply to /api/art/file/{sha1}, which needs no auth. ArtworkPolicy now decides:

  • HTTPS server -> URI only. The host fetches it, so browsing costs no HTTP calls and no bitmaps cross the binder.
  • Cleartext server -> bytes, as before. The Auto host is a separate app with its own network security config and does not permit cleartext, so an http:// icon URI would silently fail to load there.

The URI path has not been verified against a real head unit yet — that needs DHU or a car. Requested size dropped 400 -> 320 px.

docs.title: Service
docs.text:
• Settings load off the main thread; everything that needs them awaits a CompletableDeferred. onCreate used runBlocking on the very path the car uses to start the service.
  • The reporting tick backs off from 500 ms to 5 s when nothing is playing.
  • Sibling nodes share payloads through a 45 s TtlCache — the three Recently Played folders plus Recently Added were five /api/home sub-requests each.
  • onConnect filters controllers (ControllerAccess): self, platform-trusted callers, and a verified package allowlist (Auto, Assistant, system UI, Bluetooth, Wear). The service is exported, so it was previously bindable by any installed app.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Layer Where Needs a device Media id grammar, paging, cache, resume state, connection filter, artwork policy app/src/test/.../playback/ no Browse tree against a fake Jamarr server app/src/androidTest/.../JamarrLibraryProviderInstrumentedTest.kt yes Real MediaBrowser -> service plumbing app/src/androidTest/.../MediaBrowserHarnessTest.kt yes

android/scripts/emulator.sh start|stop|status boots the headless AVD (creating and fixing up its config on first use). RUN_ANDROID_INSTRUMENTATION=1 ./test.sh now boots it automatically when no device is attached and shuts it down afterwards.

The harness earned its keep immediately: the session callback was first written with Kotlin interface delegation (by), which does not generate overrides for Java default methods — so every browse call fell through to media3's defaults and returned ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED. Only a real MediaBrowser could see that.

docs.title: Playback, downloads and Android Auto hardening - 2026-10-29
docs.text: One pass over the Android issues #320, #321, #323, #324, #326, #327, #328,

docs.title: 329, #330, #331 and #333. Each landed as its own commit; this section is the
docs.text: map. The local playback and download items below were driven by hand on the headless emulator with the app signed in to the LAN server. The Android Auto items were tested two ways: the instrumented provider tests run against a fake server with canned JSON, and SignedInLibraryWalkTest walks the tree over a real MediaBrowser against the signed-in library (results under "Against the real library" below). Nothing in this pass was run inside Android Auto itself: no Desktop Head Unit, no car. How a host renders the tree, search, buttons, style hints or content:// artwork is unseen.

docs.title: Local playback
docs.text:
• Audio focus, becoming-noisy, wake mode (#323). The ExoPlayer is built with USAGE_MEDIA/CONTENT_TYPE_MUSIC attributes and ExoPlayer-managed focus, pauses on AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY, and holds WAKE_MODE_NETWORK only while playing (PlayerAudioConfig, WAKE_LOCK permission). Verified with a simulated incoming call on the emulator: focus loss paused, regain resumed. Remote renderers are untouched: UPnP and Cast never go through this player.
  • Terminal errors (#326). onPlayerError now runs PlaybackErrorPolicy: classify from the error code plus the HTTP status behind it, then retry with backoff (1 s / 3 s / 8 s, three per track per two minutes), with a fresh stream token for 401/403, a cache purge and re-download for unreadable bytes on disk, or a quality step-down for decoder trouble on an original; skip missing/unsupported tracks (three in a row at most); otherwise give up and leave the player in its error state. The queue, index and position survive because the player is only re-prepared. PlaybackDiagnostics keeps a 40-entry in-memory record with tokens and signed URLs redacted; the phone shows the summary in the banner and a Retry control in Now Playing, the car gets a readable SessionError. Verified on the emulator by cutting all networks mid-queue: three retries, gave up, Retry after the network came back resumed the same position.
  • Streaming quality ceilings (#328). One cap per network class (StreamingQualityPolicy, settings "Streaming quality"), keyed on isActiveNetworkMetered so a metered hotspot is metered. Boundary rules: a new queue starts at the cap for its network; a lower cap applies at once (reloading the current track at its position unless it is already on the device, then only what follows changes); a higher cap applies from the next queue so read-ahead on disk is not refetched. Defaults are "original" on both, which is what playback did before. Verified on the emulator: Wi-Fi off mid-album moved the next track to Opus 128.
  • Playback details (#333). Tap the quality badge in Now Playing (local playback only) for source / decoder / output layers gathered from AnalyticsListener (onAudioInputFormatChanged, onAudioDecoderInitialized, onAudioTrackInitialized, onAudioUnderrun) and an AudioDeviceCallback for the route. PlaybackDetails.processing() infers only what the numbers support (server transcode, resample, re-quantise, offload, mixer rate, underruns); unknown fields read "not reported"; the pre-API-33 route is marked as a guess. The sheet also lists the last diagnostics and offers "Copy diagnostics" as the only export.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text: • Failure reasons and a storage hold (#327). DownloadFailures classifies Media3's finalException (sign-in expired, not on server, network, server, no space left, storage error) and the reason is kept in Room (schema v2, downloaded_track.failureReason) because Media3's index only remembers "failed". StorageReservePolicy keeps the larger of 500 MB and 5 % of the volume free, pausing the DownloadManager under the reserve (through the download service, so the foreground service follows the queue) and resuming 100 MB above it; Android's own low-storage signal (the smaller of 5 % / 500 MB) is a second line via DEVICE_STORAGE_NOT_LOW. Partial downloads stay resumable and nothing is ever deleted to make room. JamarrDownloads.hold tells waiting apart from failure; the Downloads screen shows the hold, each failed row says why, its trailing control retries, and "Retry all / Retry failed" requeue the retryable ones. Verified on the emulator by filling the data partition mid-download: held at 227 MB free, resumed after the file was deleted, all 31 tracks finished. During a hold the download notification is gone (Media3 stops the service when no task runs); the in-app banner is the signal.

docs.title: Android Auto
docs.text:
• Search (#324). onSearch/onGetSearchResult are implemented and forwarded explicitly through the service callback; the root advertises SEARCH_SUPPORTED. Results are one flat bounded list in group order (artists, albums, playlists, tracks) with group-title hints, from /api/search plus playlists matched by name. Track results name the search as their parent (search:<urlencoded query>) so a tap queues the other results. A query superseded by a newer one from the same browser never announces its count. Voice play-from-search is still rejected.
  • Session buttons and style hints (#329). MediaButtonPolicy publishes shuffle, repeat and a favourite-album button (tracks cannot be favourites in Jamarr) as media button preferences, rebuilt from confirmed state on every change. The commands are session commands authorised only for controllers onConnect accepts and handled in onCustomCommand. Track items carry their album id in extras. The root declares CONTENT_STYLE_SUPPORTED; album/artist/playlist folders hint a grid, track folders a list; the host still decides the layout.
  • Targeted invalidation (#330). LibraryChanges (on the application) is the one channel for changes made on this phone: favourite toggles (screens and the session button), plays that will land in history (same 30 s / 20 % rule the server applies, device/server-renderer track changes, offline upload), playlists. LibraryChangeRouter maps each change to the cache keys to drop and the folders to re-notify; the provider batches a burst for 300 ms, invalidates before notifying, and never re-notifies an unaffected folder. Server-originated changes were evaluated and left on the TTL: the server's event stream only carries scan events.
  • Artwork content provider (#331). Browse items no longer embed image bytes. ArtworkContentProvider serves content://<pkg>.artwork/art/<sha1> and /grid/<sha1,...>: offline store first, then its own cache (cacheDir/auto_art, 48 MB, oldest out), then one bounded, single-flight server fetch published by temp-file + rename. Only artwork hashes parse; everything else is FileNotFoundException. The service grants a prefix read grant to each accepted controller. ArtworkPolicy is now URI (HTTPS) or CONTENT (cleartext server, and always for downloaded art). Not verified on a head unit (no DHU here); this is the UAMP reference approach.
  • First-page latency (#321). Before/after measured with BrowseLatencyBenchmarkTest (fake server, 40 ms per request, 2,000-row nodes, 20-row pages); the real-library numbers are in the next section:
node before after Recently Played › Albums 5 requests, ~418 ms, capped at 30 rows 1 request, ~47 ms, no cap Recently Played › Artists 5 requests, ~418 ms, capped at 30 rows 1 request, ~52 ms, no cap Recently Added 5 requests, ~414 ms, capped at 30 rows 1 request, ~51 ms, no cap Recently Played › Tracks 1 request, ~74 ms, capped at 50 rows 1 request, ~76 ms, no cap Favourite Artists 1 request, ~121 ms 1 request, ~99 ms

The home-backed folders now read their own endpoint with a limit, climbing a prefix ladder (50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000) as the browser pages; every page slices one server-ordered prefix (2,000 rows in six requests, no gaps or duplicates). Queue construction for Recently Played tracks uses the longest listed prefix. API calls are cancellable (a browse the car moved on from stops using the network) and the browse cache is bounded to 256 LRU entries. Nodes without server paging remain one request.

docs.title: Against the real library
docs.text:
SignedInLibraryWalkTest connects a MediaBrowser to the service from the app's own process and walks the tree the way a host would: every root folder in full, a sample two deep (artist → albums → tracks), paging until a short page, the artwork behind the rows through the content resolver, getItem for sampled playables, and search with names taken from the tree itself. It skips unless the installed debug app holds a session, so it costs nothing on a clean device. Run it on its own: the shared instrumented suite clears the stored session before it gets there, so inside android/test.sh it always skips (reported as an assumption failure, not a red build). Sign the app in on the emulator first, then

./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest \
  -Pandroid.testInstrumentationRunnerArguments.class=com.jamarr.android.playback.SignedInLibraryWalkTest
adb logcat -d -s LibraryWalk

Run on 2026-10-30 against the LAN server (prod library, 50-row pages, cold process):

node rows first page Playlists 16 589 ms (one /api/playlists call) Charts 100 over 2 pages 74 ms, then 7 ms Recently Added 300+ over 6 pages (capped) 431 ms; each ladder step (100, 200, 500) ~420 ms, cached pages < 10 ms Recently Played › Albums / Artists 50 75 ms / 74 ms Favourite Artists / Releases 7 / 5 33 ms / 12 ms History › Albums / Artists 10 / 10 2 ms / 36 ms Artist page (five groups) 14 556 ms Album 12–32 43–63 ms

Recently Added costs ~420 ms per request on the server whatever the limit, so the ladder's cost is in the number of steps, not the rows; the fake-server table above is the right read of the client change. All 14 sampled content:// artwork URIs decoded (400×400, grid tiles 320×320), six of six getItem calls answered, and search came back grouped and in order: "Portraits of Tracy" → 1 artist, 2 tracks; "Portraits" → 1 artist, 4 albums, 20 tracks; "the" → 20 artists, 1 playlist and nothing else, which is what /api/search itself returns for that query. Ten of fifty recently played artists had no artwork, a library gap rather than a client one. The test shares the app's uid, so the per-controller artwork grant is not exercised by it.

docs.title: Direct renderer queue recovery (#320)
docs.text: RendererResumeSnapshot (DataStore renderer_resume_v1) records the UPnP queue the phone drives: renderer id, track ids and display metadata, index, position, server URL and the session's JWT subject; never a stream URL. Written debounced from the controller's state, cleared by Stop and logout. On start RendererResumePolicy validates it (same server and account, under 12 h), waits for the renderer to be discovered, probes it without touching it, and asks: Take control when it is still on a track of our queue (adopts queue and index at the renderer's own position; no transport command), Resume when idle, Replace when it plays a foreign stream (the dialog says another controller may be using it). An unreachable renderer offers nothing and keeps the snapshot. Accepting re-checks the tracks against the server so deleted ones drop out. Cast was audited and left alone: the receiver owns that queue and the app already rebuilds it from the receiver's customData. The live probe/adopt path is not exercised against a real renderer in this pass; the policy and UpnpTrackSequencer.adopt are unit-tested.

docs.title: Jamarr Terminal UI (TUI)
docs.text:
A keyboard-driven terminal client for Jamarr. Mirrors the most-used parts of the SvelteKit web UI: login, search, browse, queue, history, playlists, and dual local + UPnP playback. Runs against the same /api/* endpoints as the web and Android clients — no backend changes.

The TUI is implemented under tui/ (a uv workspace member). Run it with uv run --package jamarr-tui jamarr-tui. The sections below describe its design and behaviour.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• One-process Python TUI driven by the existing FastAPI HTTP API.
  • Feature parity with the web UI for everyday playback and browsing.
  • Both playback paths supported, like the web client:
  • Local: stream via /api/stream-url/{id} to a subprocess audio player.
  • UPnP: drive the server's /api/player/* routes against a chosen UPnP renderer.
  • Renderer picker similar to the web Renderers page, listing UPnP devices exposed by /api/renderers plus a TUI-local entry.
  • ASCII-art artwork rendering for fun and offline-readable detail screens.
  • Fallback chain for the local audio backend: mpv → ffplay → fail loudly.

docs.title: Non-goals (v1)
docs.text:
• Charts, recommendations, scheduler, Last.fm admin, library scan, media quality, missing-albums, settings, scrobble admin.
  • Persistent auth (refresh token storage, OS keyring). v1 re-logs in each session.
  • Registering the TUI as a server-side "local" pseudo-renderer with state in renderer_state. The TUI's local mode is purely client-side; the server knows nothing about it.
  • Graphical artwork via Sixel/Kitty/iTerm2 image protocols.
  • Offline cache, downloads, sync.
  • Mouse-only flows. Keyboard is the primary interface; mouse is a bonus.
  • Windows-specific work. Linux/macOS terminals are the target.

docs.title: TUI framework: Textual
docs.text: Textual gives async event loops (matches httpx), declarative widgets, CSS-ish styling, screen routing, and a strong test harness. Raw curses is doable but would burn time on layout, focus, and async plumbing that Textual already solves.

docs.title: HTTP: httpx (async)
docs.text: Already in repo dependencies. Single AsyncClient with a base URL and an Authorization: Bearer header set after login.

docs.title: Audio backend (local mode)
docs.text:
Probe at startup, pick first available:

  1. mpv via --input-ipc-server=<socket>. JSON IPC for play/pause/seek/ volume/queue/observation of position. Best fit: gapless, accurate seek, programmable.
  2. ffplay. Fallback only. Limited control (no IPC), so seek/volume become best-effort and the queue is implemented by tearing down and respawning the process per track.
  3. None found → exit cleanly with a one-line error explaining what to install.

UPnP mode does not need a local audio binary.

docs.title: Artwork → ASCII
docs.text: pillow (already a root dep, but TUI gets its own copy) downsamples /api/art/file/{sha1}?max_size=200 to terminal cell dimensions, then maps luminance to a character ramp. Color via 24-bit truecolor where the terminal supports it (COLORTERM=truecolor), else 256-color, else monochrome ramp.

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
CLI flags first, then environment, then a config file:

Source Key Default --server server URL https://jamarr.darious.co.uk --username login username (optional) prompt JAMARR_URL server URL as above config file ~/.config/jamarr-tui/config.toml optional overrides

Username/password are never persisted. Password is always prompted.

docs.title: 3. Repository layout
docs.text:
New top-level tui/ as a uv workspace member. Root pyproject.toml gets a [tool.uv.workspace] entry adding tui as a member; the TUI's own pyproject.toml declares its slim dependency set.

docs.title: Why a separate pyproject.toml
docs.text:
The root project depends on asyncpg, mutagen, pychromecast, async-upnp-client, pillow, croniter, pylast, pychromecast — none of which the TUI needs.

TUI dependencies (rough):

  • textual
  • httpx
  • pillow
  • pydantic (transitively via FastAPI in the root, but we want it explicitly)

Workspace setup keeps uv sync --all-packages working from the repo root and lets TUI tests run via the existing CI shape.

docs.title: 4. API surface used
docs.text: Only existing endpoints. Documented in docs/api.md; re-listed here so the TUI's coupling to the backend is explicit.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text: • POST /api/auth/login — username + password, returns access token. v1 ignores the refresh cookie because the TUI is a non-browser client; on 401, prompt to re-login.

docs.title: Search and library
docs.text:

  • GET /api/stream/{track_id}?token= — handed straight to the local audio backend.
